subject: Vocabulary
description: High-frequency phrasal verbs from SSC, banking, RRB PYQ

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'CALL OFF': 'The match was called off due to rain.'

options.option_text: Postponed to a later date possibly
Cancelled and not rescheduled
Started early before time
Continued normally despite weather

questions.explanation: CALL OFF = cancel / abandon (esp. an event already planned). 'Call off the wedding', 'call off the strike'. Note distinction: CALL OFF = cancel (not happening at all). POSTPONE = delay to a later date (will happen later). PUT OFF = postpone (also delay something disliked). CALL OUT = challenge or summon publicly.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'BEAR OUT': 'The data bears out our hypothesis.'

options.option_text: Contradicts the claim made
Supports / confirms the claim
Hides or conceals the truth from
Proves something is wrong

questions.explanation: BEAR OUT = support, confirm, prove correct. 'The witness bore out my story' = backed it up. Note other 'bear' phrasals: BEAR DOWN = press down on; BEAR UP = endure (under hardship); BEAR ON = be relevant to; BEAR WITH = be patient with. PYQ-favourite phrasal.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'GO THROUGH': 'I went through the report carefully.'

options.option_text: Reject without reading it
Examine / read carefully through
Approve immediately without check
Tear up and throw away aside

questions.explanation: GO THROUGH = examine, read, study carefully OR endure (a difficult experience). 'Go through the document' = read carefully. 'Go through hardship' = experience hardship. Other GO phrasals: GO OVER = review; GO ON = continue; GO AHEAD = proceed; GO BACK = return; GO INTO = enter or examine in detail.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'KEEP AT': 'You must keep at it to succeed.'

options.option_text: Avoid the task at all costs
Persist with effort, not giving up
Cancel the project completely
Delegate to other persons fully

questions.explanation: KEEP AT (something) = persist; continue working at; not give up. 'Keep at it!' = encouragement to persist. KEEP UP = maintain pace, continue at same level. KEEP OUT = stay out / exclude. KEEP AWAY = stay distant. KEEP ON = continue. KEEP UP WITH = match someone's progress. KEEP DOWN = control / suppress (anger, voice). All common SSC, banking, CGL phrasals.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'PUT UP WITH': 'I cannot put up with this noise any longer.'

options.option_text: Enjoy or appreciate the situation
Tolerate (often with some patience)
Increase or raise level somehow
Save aside for future use

questions.explanation: PUT UP WITH = tolerate, endure (something unpleasant). 3-part phrasal verb (rare). 'Put up with the boss's tantrums.' Other PUT phrasals: PUT OFF = postpone; PUT ON = wear / pretend; PUT OUT = extinguish (fire) / annoy; PUT AWAY = store; PUT DOWN = criticize / set down; PUT UP = host / accommodate / display.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'LET DOWN': 'He really let me down by not coming.'

options.option_text: Released gently to the ground
Disappointed (failed to meet hopes)
Helped enthusiastically and warmly
Encouraged to continue trying

questions.explanation: LET (someone) DOWN = disappoint; fail to meet expectations. 'Don't let me down!' Famous song by Beatles + Daft Punk. LET phrasals: LET OFF = excuse / release / discharge (let off the hook = excuse from blame); LET IN = allow inside; LET OUT = release / make wider / leak out; LET UP = decrease / pause (e.g., 'rain didn't let up').
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'CARRY OUT': 'The team will carry out the survey next week.'

options.option_text: Cancel the planned activity
Perform / execute the activity
Delegate to other team
Postpone to a later date

questions.explanation: CARRY OUT = perform, execute, conduct. 'Carry out orders, instructions, an investigation, an experiment.' CARRY phrasals: CARRY ON = continue; CARRY OFF = succeed at / achieve (also win a prize); CARRY OVER = transfer to next period; CARRY THROUGH = complete (esp. through difficulty); CARRY AWAY = excite emotionally ('got carried away').
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: When her regular income dried up during the lockdown, she had to fall back on her savings. What does 'fall back on' mean in this sentence?

options.option_text: to ignore a resource completely and seek new help
to rely on something kept in reserve as last option
to accumulate savings over a prolonged time period
to distribute available resources equally among others

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'fall back on' means to turn to something for support when primary options fail — here, savings serve as a backup resource. A is wrong because it implies ignoring the resource, which is the opposite. C confuses the origin of savings with their use as a reserve safety net.

questions.stem: The selection committee turned down his application despite his impressive academic record. What does 'turned down' mean?

options.option_text: to accept a proposal while setting specific conditions
to defer a decision for further review at a later time
to reject or refuse a request, proposal, or offer
to lower the ranking of a candidate in evaluation

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'turn down' means to refuse or reject outright — the committee refused his application. D is the prime distractor since 'turned down' sounds like reducing rank, but the phrase means outright refusal. A implies conditional acceptance, which is the opposite of rejection.

questions.stem: Through the thick smoke, the rescue workers could barely make out the outline of the collapsed structure. What does 'make out' mean in this context?

options.option_text: to prepare or draft an official report or document
to claim or argue something in a convincing manner
to manage a situation successfully despite difficulties
to see or discern something indistinctly with effort

questions.explanation: D is correct: in a sensory context, 'make out' means to perceive or see something with difficulty. B is the prime distractor — 'make out that' means to claim (e.g., 'he made out he was innocent') — but the smoke-and-outline context confirms perception, not argument. C means 'manage' (get along), a different phrasal sense.

questions.stem: The automobile industry will phase out petrol-driven two-wheelers across urban zones by 2030. What does 'phase out' mean?

options.option_text: to introduce a new product gradually in carefully planned stages
to discontinue something gradually in a step-by-step manner
to enforce an immediate ban without any transition time
to switch repeatedly between competing systems or sources

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'phase out' means to eliminate something step by step over time. A describes 'phase in', the antonym, making it the key distractor. C implies sudden stoppage, which contradicts the gradual, planned nature embedded in the word 'phase.'

questions.stem: The landmark Supreme Court judgment was expected to bring about a fundamental shift in how privacy laws are interpreted. What does 'bring about' mean?

options.option_text: to delay or obstruct a process through procedural maneuvers
to cause or produce a result or significant change
to formally present a matter before a judicial authority
to revive or recall a past legal precedent for current use

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'bring about' means to cause something to happen. C is a tempting distractor since courts 'bring' cases forward, but 'bring about' specifically denotes causation, not presentation. D confuses recalling a precedent with producing a new outcome.

questions.stem: The company's annual report glossed over the mounting non-performing assets, which later surfaced during regulatory scrutiny. What does 'glossed over' mean?

options.option_text: to highlight and draw attention to major financial risks
to treat something superficially so as to conceal faults
to thoroughly audit something with careful meticulous precision
to restate financial figures in a clearer and readable format

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'gloss over' means to minimise or hide the significance of something by treating it briefly. A is the opposite. C is the critical trap — 'go over carefully' sounds similar, but 'gloss over' implies deliberately superficial treatment, not thoroughness. D implies reformatting, which is unrelated.

questions.stem: Rather than resolving the ideological divide within the ruling alliance, the leaders chose to paper over the cracks before the election season. What does 'paper over' mean?

options.option_text: to expose underlying conflicts by bringing them into public view
to formally record disagreements in a binding official document
to conceal or disguise a problem without truly resolving it
to negotiate a lasting agreement acceptable to all conflicting factions

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'paper over' means to temporarily hide or mask a problem rather than fix it — the metaphor is wallpaper covering structural cracks. D is the prime distractor since 'papering over cracks in an alliance' implies reconciliation, but the phrase denotes cosmetic concealment, not genuine resolution. A is the direct opposite.
